items.title: US midterms trigger Wall Street rout: How AI sell-off is spreading beyond Big Tech to riskier stocks
points: The stock-market rout, which began soon after the opening bell on the New York Stock Exchange on Thursday, worsened as the day progressed, and by the end of the day trillions of dollars were wiped out of the market value.

A basket of the most-shorted US stocks fell nearly 8%, unprofitable technology companies declined 7.7%, and the Russell 2000 index of smaller companies dropped 4.5%, pushing it into correction territory.
The Nasdaq 100 plunged more than 6% on Thursday, its worst single-day fall since March 2020, while the S&P 500 declined 4.4%.
The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index, which tracks major chipmakers, dropped 12%, also marking its worst session since March 2020, Bloomberg reported.

items.title: UDF govt to examine 488 bar licences granted during LDF rule: Excise Minister Liju
points: Thiruvananthapuram, Keralam Excise Minister M Liju has said that the UDF government would conduct a detailed examination of 488 bar licences granted during the previous LDF government's tenure and take action if any irregularities are detected.

He was responding to allegations raised by CPI leader and former Excise Minister M B Rajesh over action taken against Excise officials for issuing licences to bars in accordance with the previous LDF government's liquor policy.
These 488 bar licences were granted over 10 years by the previous two Pinarayi Vijayan governments using the authority given to Deputy Excise Commissioners through a rule amendment, he said.
Under the 2017 amendment, 410 hotels were granted bar licences during the first LDF government and another 78 during its second term, taking the total to 488, Liju said.

Disputing Rajesh's argument that the Deputy Excise Commissioners were merely exercising their long-standing authority to renew bar licences, Liju said the cases involved establishments that had lost their licences 10 to 12 years earlier.

items.title: Maharashtra Government makes provision for ₹160 crore in 2026-27 Budget for development of primitive tribes
points: Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis speaks during a meeting with the advisory committee for ‘Viksit Maharashtra 2047 ’ at Sahyadri Guest House in Mumbai.

The package includes 130 crore reserved for primitive tribes, ₹30 crore reserved for the Pardhi community, and also provides for 100% government grant for individual and collective benefit schemes.
The ₹130 crore will be further divided and allocated as follows: ₹100 crore for basic amenities and ₹30 crore for individual and collective benefit schemes.

items.title: Tata Says iRA App Security Issues Fixed – Responds To CERT-In Warning
points: Tata Motors has issued a clarification following reports about cybersecurity vulnerabilities flagged by the Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) in its connected-car applications.
The company says the identified issues have been addressed through software updates and enhanced security measures.

In a statement shared through its official social media accounts, Tata said its assessment found no evidence of unauthorised access to or compromise of customer credentials, personal information or vehicle-related data.
CERT-In’s advisory, dated November 4, 2026, classified the vulnerabilities as High severity.
It identified affected versions as iRA 2.0 version 26.7.3 and earlier, and iRA.ev version 26.7.2 and earlier.
According to Tata Motors, mandatory updates to iRA 2.0 version 26.8.2 and iRA.ev version 26.9.1 were rolled out in August and September 2026, respectively.
This distinction matters: making an update available and having every customer install it are separate steps.

items.title: Case Against Religious Leader Dhirendra Shastri Over Lord Krishna Comments
points: A criminal defamation complaint was filed against religious preacher Dhirendra Shastri in an Agra court over his remarks about Lord Krishna, a lawyer said on Thursday.

Advocate Ajay Pratap Singh filed the complaint before the Agra Civil Court, alleging that Shastri made derogatory remarks about Lord Krishna during a religious discourse, hurting the sentiments and social standing of his descendants.
Shastri compared the physical postures of Lord Ram and Lord Krishna during a Ram Katha in Karera in Shivpuri, Madhya Pradesh.
According to the complaint, Shastri said, "Those who follow Krishna might feel bad, but Krishna is very crooked.
Even when he stands, he is bent at three places." The complainant argued that Lord Krishna was born in human form in the Dwapar Yuga and that his descendants continue to live in India.

Singh also claimed to be a descendant of Lord Krishna through his maternal side and alleged that the remarks hurt the religious sentiments of Krishna's descendants and damaged their social reputation.

items.title: Supreme Court acquits school officials in Maharashtra tribal girl’s death in 2020 pillar collapse
points: The Supreme Court has acquitted the president and hostel superintendent of a Maharashtra tribal residential school of culpable homicide charges over the death of a 12-year-old girl who was crushed when a poorly constructed pillar collapsed on her in 2020.

A bench of justices JB Pardiwala and Manmohan said the school administrators could not be held criminally responsible merely for failing to ensure proper construction of the pillar, particularly when the actual construction work had been entrusted to a…

The case arose from the February 15, 2020 incident at Prashnachinha Adivasi Ashram Shala in Mangrul Chawala in Maharashtra's Amravati district, where Bharti Belsare, a Class 7 student, died after a cement-and-brick pillar collapsed on her.
The court also made it clear that even a charge under Section 304A requires more than ordinary negligence.

Referring to the legal principle of “causa causans” -- the immediate and effective cause, the bench said criminal liability under Section 304A cannot be fastened merely because an act was a necessary condition for the eventual death.

items.title: 'Mahabharata', 'Arthashastra', 'Rajatarangini' Added To UNESCO Memory Register
points: Union Minister for Culture and Tourism Gajendra Singh Shekhawat welcomed the announcement, describing the inclusion as a moment of immense pride for the country and a landmark recognition of India's extraordinary documentary and civilisational heritage.

The inclusion of Rājataraṅgiṇī, Mahābhārata and Arthaśāstra in @UNESCO Memory of the World Asia-Pacific Regional Register is a landmark recognition of India's extraordinary documentary and civilisational heritage.
The Rajatarangini, composed by the 12th-century Kashmiri historian Kalhana, is widely regarded as one of the most important historical chronicles of medieval India.
The Mahabharata, one of the world's longest epic narratives, occupies a central position in South Asian literary, philosophical and religious traditions.

The latest inscriptions also highlight India's growing engagement with UNESCO's Memory of the World Programme, which was launched in 1992 to protect documentary heritage against loss, deterioration and collective amnesia.
India's participation in the initiative is coordinated by the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (IGNCA), designated as the country's nodal institution in 2014.

items.title: Toyota Innova HyCross Is India’s Best Selling Hybrid Car
points: The Toyota Innova HyCross was the highest-selling strong-hybrid car in September 2026, with 3,143 units dispatched to dealers.

The HyCross remained ahead of the Toyota Urban Cruiser Hyryder, which recorded 2,830 hybrids, and Maruti Suzuki Grand Vitara, with 1,067.

During the latest month, the Hyryder rose 7% while the HyCross fell sharply.
The Grand Vitara was a distant third at 1,067 units, up 34%, while the newly launched Kia Sorento delivered 947 strong hybrids and ranked fourth.
Strong-hybrid HyCross prices currently start at around Rs 26.76 lakh, ex-showroom, for the VX seven-seat variant.

items.title: Fire breaks out at four-storey commercial building in Gaffar market
points: According to DCP (Central Delhi) Rohit Rajbir Singh, the fire, reported at 1.28 a.m., originated in a ground-floor shop where mobile batteries were stored before spreading to all four floors.
Around 20–25 fire tenders, three CAT ambulances and two PCR vehicles were rushed to the spot.
The blaze has since been doused, with no casualties or injuries reported so far.
Preliminary findings suggest that overheating or overcharging of batteries could have triggered the fire.

The exact cause will be ascertained after reports from the Fire Department and Electrical Inspector, while a Forensic Science Laboratory (FSL) team will examine the building for other combustible materials.
A structural safety assessment/certificate will also be obtained from the Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) to rule out any risk to human life.

During a review of the phase-wise construction and handover plan, the Union Minister was informed that Phase-I buildings, including the OPD Registration Block, OPD Block, residential buildings and designated hostels, had been completed.
Approval has been conveyed for the procurement of 180 medical equipment items worth ₹59.41 crore, of which Notices of Award have been issued for 140 items.
Officials said academic activities, including commencement of MBBS classes, are proposed for the academic session 2027–28, beginning June–July 2027.
J&K Heath Minister Sakima Itoo, who welcomed the Union Minister, praised the Centre for its support in reinforcing the healthcare infrastructure of J&K.
“It was a matter of great happiness that the Union Health Minister, who had earlier announced 50 MBBS seats, today announced that 100 MBBS students will start classes here soon.

items.title: Violence mars third phase of Rajasthan panchayat elections
points: Polling in the third phase of panchayat elections for sarpanch and ward panch posts in 27 districts of Rajasthan on Thursday was marred by clashes, stone-pelting, allegations of bogus voting and protests at several places.
Supporters of rival candidates clashed in Sikar, Chittorgarh, and Balotra districts.

A dispute between supporters of two sarpanch candidates turned violent at Delsar village in the Nawalgarh area of Jhunjhunu district, with the two sides allegedly attacking each other with sticks and batons.
A youth from Punjab’s Hoshiarpur died in the clash, while two others sustained injuries.
At Bassi in Chittorgarh district, police resorted to a lathi charge after supporters of two candidates clashed over alleged bogus voting.
Sarpanch candidate Arun Pareek was allegedly assaulted by his rival and around 50 supporters at Bhojya Ki Dhani village panchayat.
Voting for the sarpanch post was cancelled at Ludi Jhabar village panchayat in Rajgarh panchayat samiti of Churu district after the nomination of the only candidate was rejected during scrutiny.

items.title: More checks added on EC staff in eye of storm amid row over internal dissent allegations
points: The Election Commission of India (ECI) has ordered a layer of supervision for a top official in charge of IT systems and shared key responsibilities of a senior deputy election commissioner with another officer, against the backdrop of a mounting…
The November 4 work order comes three months after a controversial July 28 order prompted two election commissioners to write to the cabinet secretary objecting to the changes.
To be sure, ECI has told the Supreme Court that the July 28 order was never implemented because of a July 30 order recalling the changes.

Senior deputy election commissioner Maneesh Garg – who issued the controversial July 28 order – retains election planning but will be assisted by deputy election commissioner Prakash Rajpurohit, who also has charge of delimitation.

The order assumed significance because it comes roughly three months after election commissioners SS Sandhu and Vivek Joshi wrote nearly identical letters to cabinet secretary TV Somanathan in an unprecedented step on July 29.

items.title: Canada’s Sovereign Wealth Fund to Start Its Retail Offering in 2027
points: (Bloomberg) -- Canada’s government plans to launch new, guaranteed securities for investors early next year to seed a sovereign wealth fund, which will be able to use the money to buy equity stakes in companies including technology firms.

The sovereign vehicle, called the Canada Strong Fund, will co-invest in projects the federal government is already involved in, such as the buildout of electrical generation capacity or other energy infrastructure.
Prime Minister Mark Carney announced the wealth fund in April but gave few details on how it would work.
Finance Minister François-Philippe Champagne’s budget on Thursday says more about the vehicle, which will have a Canada-only investment mandate.

The government will hand C$25 billion ($17.9 billion) to the fund – which hasn’t yet hired an executive team or board members – and will add the proceeds from the sale of principal-protected notes to retail investors.
The government suggested the Canada Strong notes may have maturities of five, seven or 10 years.

items.title: From ghee masala dosa to Mysore pak, Bengaluru’s favourite foods set to cost more
points: Veerendra Kamat, secretary, Bangalore Hotels Association, said, “Ghee, butter and paneer prices were increased a day ago.
Hence, tea and coffee prices in all hotels across the city, from small to big ones, have increased by ₹3 to ₹5.

Now prices of items like ghee masala dosa, kesari bath, upma, pongal, ghee rice, bisibele bath, rotis, naans, parottas and sweets like halwa will also be increased.” Mr. Kamat added, “An average price of ghee masala dosa is ₹120 to ₹130 across most of the…
Some premium hotels charge up to ₹200 also.
Other items like kesari bath, ghee rice, pongal and bisibele bath will also be increased by ₹5.

However, we will increase the price probably in December during the off-season by 3% to 5%.” Arjun P., a manager working at a famous sweet outlet that has branches across the city, said, “In our shop, special Mysore Pak made using ghee is priced at ₹473…

items.title: ED searches 12 premises linked to BLM society
points: The Enforcement Directorate (ED), Kochi Zonal Office, on Wednesday (October 4, 2026) conducted search operations on 12 premises linked to Bharath Lajhna Multi State Housing Co-operative Society Ltd. (BLMSHCS) and its founder R.
Premkumar in Ernakulam, Kozhikode, Thrissur, Thiruvananthapuram, Munnar, and Chennai under the provisions of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA).

The searches were related to the alleged misappropriation and laundering of public funds belonging to BLMSHCS by Mr. Premkumar for the acquisition of assets in his name as well as in the names of his family members.
The ED investigation was initiated on the basis of a first information report (FIR) registered by the Kerala Police against Mr. Premkumar, founding member and de facto CMD of BLMSHCS, and others.

According to the FIR, he misused his influence to divert crores of rupees belonging to the society, collected from public depositors, to the accounts of his family members and relatives for the acquisition of assets.

items.title: Keenan-Reuben murder case: The tragedy that changed a village
points: Social worker Ritasha D’souza was eight years old when Amboli, her cosmopolitan neighbourhood in Andheri West, made national headlines over the killing of two men—Keenan Santos, 24, and Reuben Fernandez, 29--for protecting their female friends from sexual…
By the time D’souza began her postgraduate studies in social work years later, “neighbourhood heroes” Keenan and Reuben had become part of the academic discourse on violence against women.

The court’s order on Thursday sentencing Rana to life imprisonment while acquitting two other men of murder, brings the curtain down on a case that tested a city which prides itself on being the safest city for women in India.
On the night of October 20, 2011, a group of seven friends—four men and three women—had gone to the Amboli Kitchen Bar and Restaurant to watch an India-England cricket match on the big screen.

items.title: Jantar Mantar July protests: Supreme Court asks enquiry panel to submit reports in a month on police crackdown, alleged brutality
points: The five-member committee, formed in August under the chairmanship of former Supreme Court judge, justice (retd) R Subhash Reddy, informed the court in a confidential report that only a few complaints had been received on the portal, with no complainant…

Posting the matter for December 2, the bench said, “The committee may submit an interim report on the priority issues identified by us.” The court asked the petitioners to encourage victims and complainants to file their representations with the committee.

The court also said that since complainants were not required to disclose victims’ identities, petitioners could share with the HPEC material already submitted before the court, including copies of petitions and video clips attached to them.
The bench said the committee had not yet begun preparing action-taken reports on the 12 issues identified by the court in its August 18 order.
The bench also clarified that its August 18 order should not be interpreted as a direction to initiate disciplinary action against police personnel found to have committed excesses.
